newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka air force jet crashes after pilot ejects.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka air force jet crashes after pilot ejects.

text.p: A Sri Lankan airforce fighter jet crashed into a lagoon in southwestern Sri Lanka on Tuesday after the pilot ejected, military officials said.
The fighter crashed as authorities searched for another missing aircraft, and was the third Sri Lankan plane lost in the past week.

"The Kfir (jet) experienced difficulties soon after takeoff from the Katunaike airbase," military spokesman Brigadier Tissa Jayatunga told Reuters. "The pilot ejected and landed safely. The machine crashed into the lagoon (near the airbase)."
Katunaike is about 25 km (16 miles) north of Colombo.
The pilot of the Israeli-built Kfir was undergoing treatment in hospital. It was not immediately clear why he ejected soon after takeoff, military officials said.
The crash occurred soon after the military reported sighting unidentified debris in waters off the northern Jaffna Peninsula while searching for a missing air force surveillance plane.

But the debris could not be retrieved and the navy and air force resumed their search for the Chinese-built Y-12 plane, missing off northern Sri Lanka since Monday, a senior air force official said. The twin-propeller aircraft had a crew of four.
Air force planes and helicopters, joined by navy patrol boats, were continuing their search for the Y-12, last seen about 75 miles (120 km) east of the military's Palaly air base, the official added.
The aircraft was looking for a suspected Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) ship when it lost radio contact with the ground on Monday.
Last week, an unmanned Israeli-built air force drone used for reconnaissance vanished over the Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) north of Colombo.
A rebel statement last Saturday said "an unmanned spy plane" had crashed in the Pooneryn area south of the Jaffna Peninsula last week "due to apparent mechanical failure".

The LTTE, which is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island, has not commented on the disappearance of the Y-12 aircraft.
